Compare transition structures between groups with a permutation test

Source: R/compare_lsa.R
compare_lsa.Rd

compare_lsa() tests whether groups of sequences (high and low achievers, courses, conditions) differ in their transition structure, transition by transition and as a whole, with a permutation test. Groups can differ in which transitions they over- or under-produce. The permutation test checks whether an observed difference between groups is larger than would arise if group membership were unrelated to the sequences: the group labels of whole sequences are shuffled many times, the models are refitted, and the observed difference is set against the differences produced by the shuffles. Because whole sequences are permuted, the dependence between events of one sequence is kept and only the link between group and transition structure is tested.

For each transition, compare_lsa() compares a per-group measure, by default the log odds ratio of the transition against all other transitions, which does not grow with the number of transitions observed, so groups of different sizes can be compared. Each transition gets the group difference, a permutation p-value (Phipson & Smyth, 2010) and an adjusted p-value; transitions too rare to be compared are left untested. An omnibus test of overall difference, the sum of squared differences over the tested transitions, is computed from the same permutations, in the spirit of the network comparison test of van Borkulo et al. (2023). With more than two groups every pair is compared and the adjust correction is applied once across the p-values of all pairs.

The groups must share their states, engine, lag and structural zeros; fitting them together with lsa(data, group = ) ensures this. For a Bayesian comparison of transition probabilities that reports the plausible size of each difference without resampling, use bayes_compare_lsa(). A difference between groups can also arise from a difference in their composition; check subgroups when such a confound is plausible.

Usage

compare_lsa(
  x,
  y = NULL,
  R = 1000L,
  measure = c("log_or", "adj_res", "yules_q", "prob", "count", "lift"),
  adjust = "none",
  min_count = 5L,
  parallel = FALSE,
  n_cores = NULL,
  verbose = FALSE,
  ...
)

Arguments

x

A grouped fit from lsa(data, group = ) with two or more groups, or the lsa fit of the first group.

y

The lsa fit of the second group when x is a single fit (the groups are then labelled "a" and "b"). Default NULL.

R

Number of label permutations per comparison. Default 1000.

measure

Per-transition measure compared between groups: "log_or" (default; log odds ratio of the transition, with 0.5 added to every cell of its 2 x 2 table when one cell is empty), "yules_q" (also independent of sample size, but bounded at -1 and 1), "adj_res" (adjusted residual; grows with the number of transitions, so a message is shown when one group has more than 1.5 times the transitions of another), "prob" (transition probability), "count" or "lift" (observed / expected count).

adjust

Multiple-comparison correction, any method of stats::p.adjust() such as "BH", "holm" or "bonferroni". Default "none".

min_count

Minimum combined count of a transition in the two groups for it to be tested. Default 5; 0 tests every transition.

parallel

Run the permutations on several cores. Default FALSE.

n_cores

Number of cores when parallel = TRUE. Default NULL, all cores but one.

verbose

Report progress. Default FALSE.

...

Not used.

Value

With two groups, an object of class c("lsa_comparison", "list"); with more than two, an object of class c("lsa_comparison_pairwise", "list"). Read the per-transition table with transitions(): one row per transition (from -> to pair), and for more than two groups one row per transition and pair of groups, with the columns

  • group_a, group_b (more than two groups only): the pair compared;

  • from, to: source and target state;

  • <measure>_a, <measure>_b (for example log_or_a): the measure in each group;

  • diff: the difference, group a minus group b;

  • p_perm: permutation p-value (NA when not tested);

  • p_adj: p-value after adjust;

  • significant: p_adj below the alpha of the fits.

transitions(x, significant = TRUE) keeps the significant transitions; sort = "strength" orders by the absolute difference. The omnibus test is read with as.data.frame(x, what = "global") (one row per pair of groups). print() shows the groups, the number of significant transitions and the omnibus test (see as.data.frame.lsa_comparison()); plot() draws the differences. The object also stores the permuted differences, the settings and the group fits.

Conditions

Errors carry the class lagdynamics_error and one of:

  • lagdynamics_needs_events: a fit was built from a transition matrix, so there are no sequences to permute.

  • lagdynamics_incompatible_fits: the groups differ in their states, engine, lag or structural zeros.

  • lagdynamics_bad_input: adjust is not a method of stats::p.adjust(); x is neither a grouped fit nor an lsa fit with a second fit in y; y is given together with a grouped fit; or the grouped fit has fewer than two groups.

References

Phipson, B., & Smyth, G. K. (2010). Permutation p-values should never be zero: Calculating exact p-values when permutations are randomly drawn. Statistical Applications in Genetics and Molecular Biology, 9(1), Article 39.

van Borkulo, C. D., van Bork, R., Boschloo, L., Kossakowski, J. J., Tio, P., Schoevers, R. A., Borsboom, D., & Waldorp, L. J. (2023). Comparing network structures on three aspects: A permutation test. Psychological Methods, 28(6), 1273-1285.

See also

transitions() and as.data.frame.lsa_comparison() to read the result; plot.lsa_comparison() to draw it; bayes_compare_lsa() for a Bayesian comparison; permute_lsa() to test one fit against no sequential structure; lsa() with group = to fit the groups.

Examples

g <- lsa(group_regulation_long, actor = "Actor", action = "Action",
         time = "Time", group = "Achiever")
cmp <- compare_lsa(g, R = 100, adjust = "BH")
cmp
#> <lsa_comparison>
#>   groups:   High vs Low
#>   measure:  log_or difference (High - Low)
#>   R:        100 label permutations
#>   edges:    36 significant of 78 tested (adjust = BH)
#>   omnibus:  statistic = 79.48, p = 0.009901
transitions(cmp, significant = TRUE, sort = "strength") |> head()
#>        from        to   log_or_a  log_or_b      diff     p_perm      p_adj
#> 1  cohesion     adapt -0.7935888 -3.920901  3.127313 0.00990099 0.02340234
#> 2   emotion synthesis -1.6186504 -4.521535  2.902885 0.00990099 0.02340234
#> 3      plan synthesis -2.1452241 -4.950504  2.805280 0.00990099 0.02340234
#> 4  cohesion synthesis -1.3553011 -3.944575  2.589274 0.00990099 0.02340234
#> 5 synthesis   monitor -3.2285363 -0.974550 -2.253986 0.00990099 0.02340234
#> 6 synthesis      plan -0.5805673 -2.680438  2.099871 0.00990099 0.02340234
#>   significant
#> 1        TRUE
#> 2        TRUE
#> 3        TRUE
#> 4        TRUE
#> 5        TRUE
#> 6        TRUE
as.data.frame(cmp, what = "global")
#>   group_a group_b statistic    p_value   R
#> 1    High     Low  79.47723 0.00990099 100
# \donttest{
# A full analysis uses more permutations
compare_lsa(g, R = 1000, adjust = "BH")
#> <lsa_comparison>
#>   groups:   High vs Low
#>   measure:  log_or difference (High - Low)
#>   R:        1000 label permutations
#>   edges:    39 significant of 78 tested (adjust = BH)
#>   omnibus:  statistic = 79.48, p = 0.000999

# Three courses: every pair, corrected across all pairs
courses <- lsa(group_regulation_long, actor = "Actor", action = "Action",
               time = "Time", group = "Course")
compare_lsa(courses, R = 100, adjust = "BH") |>
  as.data.frame(what = "global")
#>   group_a group_b statistic    p_value      p_adj
#> 1       A       B 57.753343 0.00990099 0.01485149
#> 2       A       C 55.297067 0.00990099 0.01485149
#> 3       B       C  8.364228 0.75247525 0.75247525
# }
